title: Pre-shot actions
lead: Which actions and chains of actions precede better chances, how they change the defense's shape, and how spacing relates to outcomes.

blocks.text: Which actions, and which orders of actions, come before the best chances? Each half-court chance is reduced to the list of actions SkillCorner marked in it (picks, handoffs, off-ball screens, drives, isolations, post-ups, closeouts), plus the site's basket cuts and paint touches, in the order they happened, up to the shot. Outcomes are the chance's points, shot quality (xPts per FGA), turnovers, free-throw trips and offensive rebounds on live misses.

Actions are SkillCorner's detections plus the site's cuts; both miss some actions and mislabel others. A long chain is also a long chance, and the shot clock forces shots late in long chains, so counts and orders are confounded with time.

blocks.text: Spacing at release is tied to where the shot is: a layup puts the shooter (and his defender) in the key. The chance-average view is less tied to the shot spot but still reflects the opponent and the lineup.

sections.title: What this shows and does not

blocks.text: It shows which actions and short sequences come before better and worse chances, and how each action moves the defense in the next two seconds. It does not separate the action from who runs it, against whom, or how much time was left.

If this becomes the topic: model the chance outcome on the last action with team and opponent terms; use the shape changes (hull, key, room off the ball) as the mechanism, and test whether an action that shrinks the defense more leads to a better next shot.
